name: Political correctness
summary: Political correctness names language, policies or measures meant to avoid offence to groups that suffer prejudice or discrimination (by race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation or disability). The defining sources trace it from a dogmatism jibe in 1930s-50s communist politics, through ironic self-description on the 1970s-80s New Left, to a mostly pejorative label from the 1990s that conservatives applied to the left. They describe a practice about speech and manners, not a programme for government, economy or foreign policy, so they state no position on almost every statement.
scope: The sense the defining sources give the term: language, policies and measures that avoid offence to disadvantaged groups (Hamilton, New World Encyclopedia, Chow for NPR). Positions that critics attribute to it (censorship, orthodoxy) and the programmes of the feminist, anti-racist and multiculturalist movements it is applied to are other subjects and add no answers.
